title: Expected Number of Shared Birthday Pairs

problemStatement.formal: E[number of pairs sharing a birthday] = C(n,2)/365 = n(n-1)/730
problemStatement.plain: In a group of n people with uniformly distributed birthdays, what is the expected number of pairs who share a birthday?
whyMatters: Natural extension of the birthday problem from probability to expectation
Demonstrates linearity of expectation in formal mathematics
Connects combinatorial counting to expected value

open: Formal connection to MeasureTheory.Probability (indicator random variables)
Variance of shared pairs: Var = C(n,2) * (1/365) * (364/365) + correlations
knownResults.goal: Prove expected number of shared birthday pairs formula and threshold

currentState.focus: Core results already formalized in BirthdayProblem.lean Part VII.
currentState.nextAction: None - core problem completed. Extensions possible via probability theory.

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: Expected shared pairs formula C(n,2)/365 fully formalized in BirthdayProblem.lean (Part VII, lines 304-356). Includes definition, specific values (n=0,1,2,23), threshold at n=28 (>1 expected pair), tight lower bound at n=27, and nonnegativity proof.
insights: Linearity of expectation makes the formula trivial: each of C(n,2) pairs has independent 1/365 chance
The combinatorial formulation avoids measure theory entirely
28 is the threshold where we expect >1 shared pair (vs 23 for >50% probability of any match)
All proofs use norm_num and Nat.choose - no native_decide needed for expected values
mathlibGaps: No formal linearity of expectation for discrete uniform distributions in Lean 4
Indicator random variable framework would formalize the derivation
nextSteps: Could extend with variance computation: Var[X] = C(n,2)/365 * 364/365 + correction terms
Could connect to MeasureTheory.Probability for formal probabilistic derivation

approaches.name: Direct combinatorial definition
approaches.description: Define E[pairs] = C(n,2)/365 directly and prove specific values and thresholds using norm_num
